hypotheses: By itself, every run: a run ends by opening the issues it filed as debug cases, running the debug workflow on them, merging the fixes through plumb's merge check and running the task once more (--rounds N for more fix rounds; --rounds 0 only documents the issues); the owner is asked through the question tool only when a fix would change the intent or a requirement's meaning, or the merge check holds a fix
records.premise:
/plumb:plumb intent I want a very cheap way to stress test plumb. I want Haiku to use plumb and develop a simple playable game. Or feel free to find a relevant benchmark. Actually there could be a rather complex task and one quite simple game. The idea is to be able from one plumb dev command like plumb evaluate simple or plumb evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using plumb tools. when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb

Question: When plumb evaluate runs and the model finds an issue, should plumb act on it itself (fix it on a branch and run the benchmark again), or should it only write the issue to a file for you to use later?

You said on 2026-10-21: "when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb"
Options: Only write the issue to a file (Recommended) (Issues are kept in a file for later reuse. Nothing is fixed or rerun automatically. Recommended: You asked that issues be written to a file that you can later re-use, which describes keeping them for later rather than fixing them on the spot.); Fix each issue on a branch, then rerun (After each run, plumb fixes the issues on a branch and runs the benchmark again, up to a set number of rounds.)
Answer: Evaluate just documents the issues. but then debug is called to work on those issues, and ensure plumb compliant merge of the fixes. Of course it should come back to the user with question tool when fixing implies changing the intent 

Question: When plumb evaluate's merge check holds a fix, should plumb stop and report why, or should it ask you through the question tool what to do?

You said on 21 Oct: "Of course it should come back to the user with question tool when fixing implies changing the intent"
Options: Stop and report why (Recommended) (The run ends and names why the merge check held the fix. You decide the next step. No question is sent to you. Recommended: You asked to be asked through the question tool when fixing implies changing the intent. A merge the check holds is not that case, so stopping and reporting matches your words.); Ask me through the question tool (The run pauses and sends you a question about the held fix before it goes on.)
Answer: Stop and report why (Recommended)
